problem_summary.summary: Find the two distinct array positions whose values add to a target; the input guarantees one solution.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: integer array nums and integer target. Return the two matching indices in either order.
constraints: Exactly one valid answer exists; an element cannot be used twice

brute_force.explanation: Try every pair of distinct indices and return the first pair whose values sum to target.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The nested loops enumerate every legal pair, so the guaranteed solution is eventually checked.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^2) worst case, checking each pair.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary, excluding the returned two-index array.

optimized.explanation: Scan once while storing each previously seen value and its index. For the current value, look up target minus that value before storing the current element.
optimized.correctness_idea: At index i, the map contains exactly earlier indices. If the complement is present, that earlier value and the current value form a valid pair of distinct positions. Every solution is found when its later index is scanned.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) expected, with one pass and expected constant-time hash map operations.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for previously seen values and their indices.

steps.condition: Complement 2 is not in the map.
Complement 7 is not in the map.
Complement 4 is not in the map.

edge_cases.handling: The earlier occurrence is stored before the later one is checked.
Integer complements work for negative numbers within the stated bounds.

edge_cases.case: Solution occurs at the last position
edge_cases.handling: The complement lookup is performed before that position is stored, so only distinct indices can match.
